newsitem.title: FRANCE: Speculation on EMU first wave "illusory" - Santer.
newsitem.headline: Speculation on EMU first wave "illusory" - Santer.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Sunday that it was "illusory and unfounded" to speculate on which European Union member states would take part in the first wave of monetary union in 1999.

EU member states are invited to become candidates "on the condition that they fulfill the convergence criteria, that is the Maastricht criteria, and it's up to the heads of state of the governments to make the selection in the spring of 1998 on the basis of the criteria," he told radio RTL.

"So at this time, it seems absolutely illusory and unfounded to speculate on who will enter, the names of the countries that will enter, those which will not enter, etc. Let's let our governments, the member states, do their work to attain the criteria," he said.
Asked in the radio interview about reports of a secret report envisaging a delayed entry for Spain and Italy, Santer said he was not aware of any such secret report.
He also said the choice of who would head the new European Central Bank would not be decided on the basis of nationality but on the basis of the candidate's qualifications.

Asked about Jacques Delors, the former Commission president, Santer said Delors had "all the qualifications." He said candidates included Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg, set to take over as head of the European Monetary Institute in July, succeeding Alexandre Lamfalussy.

"It's not a question of nationality," Santer said. "Let's be clear. It's a question of who is effectively the most capable person, and that the (EU) heads of state and governments or the council of ministers appreciate (that person) as such, to manage the European Central Bank."
He said the future European currency should be strong and credible to stand up to the dollar and the yen, but he said the exchanges rates would be determined by the capital markets.
